investigation.title: api-health eval failure: Cloudflare 522 connection timeout to origin host api.aura.ai
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for check api-health failed because GET /health on the production-api origin (api.aura.ai) returned a Cloudflare 522 Connection Timed Out error, meaning Cloudflare's network successfully received the request but could not establish a TCP connection to the origin server within the timeout window. The eval runner received an HTML error page instead of a JSON payload, so the required evidence key "status" was never populated and the expected-output contract assertion { path: "status", equals: "ok" } could not be satisfied.
investigation.rootCause: The origin server at api.aura.ai failed to accept or respond to Cloudflare's inbound TCP connection during the eval window (2026-07-21T18:45:06Z–18:45:45Z). Cloudflare's diagnostic page explicitly marks the browser and Cloudflare PoP (Los Angeles) as "Working" and the host (api.aura.ai) as "Error", localizing the fault to the origin tier. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1178) calls publicJson(args.baseUrl, "/health") and received a 522 HTML response instead of a JSON object, leaving the evidence map empty and triggering the contract gap on the "status" key. This is an eval-detected origin connectivity failure scoped to the /health endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
proof: failed-check.message: GET /health returned HTTP 522 with a Cloudflare 'Connection timed out' HTML page; the Cloudflare error page explicitly shows host api.aura.ai in Error state while browser and Cloudflare PoP are Working.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=38986, which is 7.8× the outageLatencyMs threshold of 5000ms defined in infra/evals/status/features.json line 31 (source.infra/evals/status/features.json:31), confirming the request hung until Cloudflare's own timeout fired.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty {}; no JSON body was parsed from the response.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: required evidence key 'status' is absent, violating the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 6–7 (source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:1-8).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1172-1180: runner at line 1178 calls publicJson(args.baseUrl, '/health') and at line 1179 evaluates response?.status === 'ok'; a non-JSON 522 response yields a null/undefined response object, so evidence is null and the check fails.

sibling.auth-session and sibling.system-info both passed in the same run window (latencyMs 790ms and 357ms respectively), indicating the broader production-api runtime was reachable for authenticated and system-info routes, isolating the failure to the /health endpoint or its specific origin process/port binding.
possibleCauses: Origin server process crash or restart: the /health handler process on api.aura.ai was down or restarting at the time of the eval, causing Cloudflare to time out. Sibling checks passing on other routes slightly weakens but does not eliminate this if /health is served by a different process or port.

Origin firewall or security group blocking Cloudflare IPs on the /health route specifically: a network-layer rule could selectively drop connections to the health endpoint while allowing authenticated API traffic through a different path or IP allowlist.

Cloudflare origin connection pool exhaustion or misconfigured keepalive timeout: the origin closed idle connections faster than Cloudflare's keepalive interval, causing the 522 specifically for the unauthenticated /health probe while authenticated routes succeeded via a different connection path.

Transient origin overload or cold-start on a serverless/container platform (the error page title references onrender.com, suggesting a Render.com-hosted service): the origin container may have been spinning up or under resource pressure at the moment of the eval, causing the TCP handshake to stall.

Misconfigured baseUrl in the eval runner args pointing to an origin that no longer serves /health: if args.baseUrl resolves to a host that has been decommissioned or re-routed, only the /health probe would fail while other checks using different base URLs or authenticated paths succeed.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: The remote-agent-create eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: all 6 nodes in the production cluster were either exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes) or excluded by pod affinity/node selector rules (4 nodes). This caused the pod to remain unschedulable for 120 seconds, terminating before any VM was assigned and leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) completely absent. All three remote-agents checks failed concurrently, with the sibling remote-agent-runtime check additionally receiving a Cloudflare 522 connection timeout against api.aura.ai, indicating the production API host was also unreachable during the same window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, the agent pod could not be scheduled within the 120-second window. Because the pod never started, no VM was allocated, no agent identity was created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the remote-agent-create contract. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes and affinity mismatch on the remaining 4, leaving zero schedulable nodes. This is the direct cause reported by the Kubernetes scheduler (failed-check.message).

CONTRIBUTING — concurrent or recently created remote agents consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the matching nodes, leaving no capacity for the eval probe's pod. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, suggesting all existing pods are non-preemptible.

CONTRIBUTING — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool scaling issue: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized or the affinity rules are overly restrictive, capacity headroom is structurally limited.

SECONDARY — api.aura.ai origin server unreachable via Cloudflare (522) during the same window (sibling.remote-agent-runtime): this may indicate the API server itself was overloaded or restarting, which could be a downstream effect of the same infrastructure pressure or an independent event. No causal link is proven by the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster metrics show that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were available and unused on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.

If the eval re-runs successfully immediately after the failure without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held lock or a pod that was terminating) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for check api-health failed because GET /health on the production-api origin (api.aura.ai) returned a Cloudflare 522 Connection Timed Out error, meaning Cloudflare's network successfully received the request but could not establish a TCP connection to the origin server within the timeout window. The eval runner received an HTML error page instead of a JSON payload, so the required evidence key "status" was never populated and the expected-output contract assertion { path: "status", equals: "ok" } could not be satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The origin server at api.aura.ai failed to accept or respond to Cloudflare's inbound TCP connection during the eval window (2026-07-21T18:45:06Z–18:45:45Z). Cloudflare's diagnostic page explicitly marks the browser and Cloudflare PoP (Los Angeles) as "Working" and the host (api.aura.ai) as "Error", localizing the fault to the origin tier. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1178) calls publicJson(args.baseUrl, "/health") and received a 522 HTML response instead of a JSON object, leaving the evidence map empty and triggering the contract gap on the "status" key. This is an eval-detected origin connectivity failure scoped to the /health endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Origin server process crash or restart: the /health handler process on api.aura.ai was down or restarting at the time of the eval, causing Cloudflare to time out. Sibling checks passing on other routes slightly weakens but does not eliminate this if /health is served by a different process or port.

Origin firewall or security group blocking Cloudflare IPs on the /health route specifically: a network-layer rule could selectively drop connections to the health endpoint while allowing authenticated API traffic through a different path or IP allowlist.

Cloudflare origin connection pool exhaustion or misconfigured keepalive timeout: the origin closed idle connections faster than Cloudflare's keepalive interval, causing the 522 specifically for the unauthenticated /health probe while authenticated routes succeeded via a different connection path.

Transient origin overload or cold-start on a serverless/container platform (the error page title references onrender.com, suggesting a Render.com-hosted service): the origin container may have been spinning up or under resource pressure at the moment of the eval, causing the TCP handshake to stall.

Misconfigured baseUrl in the eval runner args pointing to an origin that no longer serves /health: if args.baseUrl resolves to a host that has been decommissioned or re-routed, only the /health probe would fail while other checks using different base URLs or authenticated paths succeed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigations.summary: The remote-agent-create eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: all 6 nodes in the production cluster were either exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes) or excluded by pod affinity/node selector rules (4 nodes). This caused the pod to remain unschedulable for 120 seconds, terminating before any VM was assigned and leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) completely absent. All three remote-agents checks failed concurrently, with the sibling remote-agent-runtime check additionally receiving a Cloudflare 522 connection timeout against api.aura.ai, indicating the production API host was also unreachable during the same window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, the agent pod could not be scheduled within the 120-second window. Because the pod never started, no VM was allocated, no agent identity was created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the remote-agent-create contract. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.
